correctness.rationale: For a constant gradient and frozen orthogonal basis, both SOAP EMAs converge entrywise to their constant-signal limits, so the stationary normalized coordinate is exactly \(F_\varepsilon(z)=z/(|z|+\varepsilon)\). For the \(45^\circ\) family the stale update is \(\begin{bmatrix}p&r\\r&p\end{bmatrix}\), whose singular values are \(p\pm r\); direct algebra gives the stated condition number and smallest singular value. Refreshing to the true eigenbasis diagonalizes the signal and gives the stated fresh spectrum. The general angle formula follows from the exact rotated off-diagonal entry.

value.rationale: Basis freshness is now a documented practical stability issue for SOAP, and epsilon is a documented numerical stability parameter. The result connects them quantitatively: it gives an exact singular-value collapse, an explicit \(1/arepsilon\) conditioning law, and a sharp angle at which an off-diagonal stale coordinate reaches half of its saturated Adam normalization. These are natural spectral invariants of the optimizer's defining matrix update and provide a precise mechanism for why a seemingly small basis lag can matter.
